item.title: Re: Box of Miscellaneous Items
item.content:encoded: I like the idea of showing the foundation isn't perfect, but I'm not sure this is the right way to do it. I feel like the foundation would be glad that an object that they thought was anomalous isn't, and they definitely wouldn't label a normal box Keter. This might work better as a tale than an article. Maybe you could center it around a single researcher who gets driven insane by the box and his own pride? Just some ideas.

item.title: Box of Miscellaneous Items
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: no

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional i guess

Page Layout (Optional): Pictures, story, tabs for testing and the like.

Elevator Pitch: Additional Notes: Note any concerns or particular areas of assistance you would like reviewers to focus on.I have an idea, but not sure how good it is so I want some advice. The skip is legit a cardboard box of random items. Every person swears the box is anomalous. But nothing happens, no sensor readings, no properties, nothing. It is, for all purposes, a random box with random goods inside. Just a plain old box. Yet, the Foundation- in all their wisdom and favor- cannot accept that they might have gotten one wrong. So its classified as either keter since the foundation starts associating random mundane everyday bad luck with it just to make some sense of it.

Pretty much, I want to tell this story of the Foundation being so zealous and confident that they cannot accept that they made a single mistake somewhere and have been wasting time on an ordinary box.

Central Narrative: Its going to describe the long and turtourus experience of many researchers attempting to prove that this box is anomalous. From scanners to shoving the box in with other skips, to eventual word of mouth fear of the box and its supposed properties. Eventually with high clearance the story will be shown that more and more tests came back negative, until only the O-5 council access shows it is a normal box but the council cannot admit it was a mistake.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I want to tell the story not of the Foundation being perfect, but rather as a flawed machine that thinks its perfect. Of thinking they cannot even make a single mistake.
